autonomy.chose: The stamp is one `recorded` object in the filed review, { reviewer, via, reelplanning }, where `via` says whether the reviewer came from the page's viewer or git's user.email; the same review filed again with a different stamp (another person's intake, an upgrade) is still the same review, not a second file
autonomy.insteadOf: top-level reviewer and version fields, or a file beside the review
autonomy.why: the filed review is the player's export plus what intake adds; one key keeps the two apart, and a refile must not turn one review into two

autonomy.chose: The version is the reelplanning that records the review (its package.json)
autonomy.insteadOf: the version that built the video, as the plan says
autonomy.why: no build writes which version built a video (video/meta.json has none); with the pinned npx or this checkout, the two are the same version

autonomy.chose: migrate-reviews files old reviews unstamped (stamp: false)
autonomy.insteadOf: stamping them with whoever runs the migration
autonomy.why: old reviews stay as they are: who recorded them then is not known, and today's email and version would be wrong

autonomy.chose: The five lines' ids are words: recommended, own-words, rewinds, checks, misses (and flagged for yours across repos), so `reel memory own-words` says what it prints
autonomy.why: an id you type is easier to remember as a word, and it stays the same when a line has nothing to say and is left out

autonomy.chose: Why a question was answered in own words is read from the words and the options: 'unclear, asked for more', 'an option, with a condition', otherwise 'the question framed otherwise'; the words are always shown with it
autonomy.insteadOf: no reason, only the words; or a reason the reviewer picks
autonomy.why: the plan's own problem statement sorts D-022, D-003 and D-023 this way, and all three land where it put them; a heuristic that shows its evidence can be wrong in the open

autonomy.chose: 'Rewound again after a revision' is the same step of the same plan's same video rewound or slowed in two different reviews of it; a rewind with no step is left out of the line
autonomy.insteadOf: counting rewinds twice within one review; or including rewinds with no step
autonomy.why: a second review of a video is what follows a revision; two rewinds in one sitting are one hard part, and a moment with no step cannot be said about any step

autonomy.chose: Your file (~/.reelplanning/you.jsonl) gets a summary only for a review recorded inside a git repo (the repo is named by its git top level), once per repo, plan and review, and `reel record` says so on one line each time ('a summary of this review added to …', 'already in …', or 'not in a git repo')
autonomy.insteadOf: a summary for every review recorded anywhere
autonomy.why: a summary names its repo, and outside git there is none to name; it also keeps the player's finish.spec (a scratch folder, no git) out of the real home; the line makes it plain what reached the file. Each line names its reviewer: in a cloud session that is git's user.email (noreply@anthropic.com here) until the page sends a viewer (A7)

autonomy.chose: Across repos (`reel memory --you`) the fifth line is `flagged`, the kinds of call flagged or answered in own words, by tag, instead of misses
autonomy.why: a miss is found in a repo's ledger history (what superseded what, rows changed after review), which a one-line summary per review does not carry; the plan's step 3 lists the kinds of call flagged as what the summary holds

autonomy.chose: Where your file cannot be written (a run fenced to the repo by D-082's sandbox, a read-only home), `reel record` records the review all the same and says, on its last line, that this one is not in your memory
autonomy.insteadOf: failing the record; or keeping a pending copy in the repo to add later
autonomy.why: recording the review is the job; the summary is a copy, and a pending file in the repo would be one more thing kept by hand

autonomy.chose: A miss is recent while the plan that showed it is one of the last five plan folders, retros not counted
autonomy.insteadOf: a number of days, or until the next retro
autonomy.why: plans are the unit the retro rule already counts (D-107), and days mean nothing in a repo worked on in bursts; on this repo it keeps D-056 → D-063 and m3's step 6, and lets close-the-lifecycle's two go

autonomy.chose: A call's kind is its tags and the components its step names; a recent miss stops a tagged call that shares a tag with it, or, when the miss has no tags (a plan question, or a call logged before tags), a component. An untagged call still never stops (D-084). Right now no miss has tags, so D-056 → D-063 (component player) stops every tagged player call: all 22 of answer-on-the-video's calls, and m3's step 6 stops 13 of this plan's 15
autonomy.insteadOf: tags only (every miss so far has none, so nothing would change); or making untagged calls stop too
autonomy.why: the plan traces a question's miss to its components, so a component is the only way such a miss can reach a call; untagged calls are the ones the agent judged a reviewer would not care about, and the streak is what the exception overrides

autonomy.chose: 'A part reworked soon after' is read as a step whose walkthrough quick check the reviewer disagreed with in their own words (it worked otherwise than the plan they approved led them to expect, and was reworked), traced to that step's plan questions; a call accepted in review whose row later says '(changed after review: …)' counts as an accepted call reversed. autonomy.chose: A signal is one of: a question answered in own words for the same reason, a step rewound again after a revision, a quick check answered wrong on the same component, a miss of the same kind (tag, else component), a call flagged with the same tag; each counted over the plans since the last retro, and three of one makes a retro due

autonomy.chose: `reel retro` names its folder <date>-retro (then -retro-2 …); its draft cites the active plan decisions on the skill as in force, so `reel check` passes it as written; the benchmark's parts are found by their files, in the repo or else in reelplanning's own checkout

calls.why: the plan asks intake to use a viewer when the row has one; the player is being changed elsewhere right now, and a row that carries one works as soon as a page sends it
calls.check: scripts/lib/reviews.mjs recordedBy; scripts/reel-intake.mjs passes the row

calls.chose: A call counts once, by the first verdict it was given (a later round that re-judges it does not count again); plan questions count per review

frames.title: What ran; flag a step, or accept

plan.title: Memory: learn which questions are the right ones, from what reviews already record
plan.problem:
Every plan starts from nothing. The records say a lot about what you care about, but no plan reads
them. You took the recommended option on every question you answered from a list, and wrote your
own words on 3 of 16: the options were too abstract (D-022), the question was framed wrong (D-023),
or you accepted with a condition (D-003). You accepted 85 of 91 of the agent's calls. The steps you
rewound are the ones you later flagged or questioned, and one was rewound again after its revision.
Most of your own-words notes are questions. And some things got past a review and were changed
later: a decision superseded (D-056 by D-063), a call accepted and reversed after review (the
file tools, k3), a part reworked within days. Each of those is a question that should have been
asked, or a call that should have stopped.

The aim is the right questions, not fewer. The tool can also improve itself, which needs a
yardstick outside its own numbers: it could "improve" by asking less and counting that as success.

steps.title: Every review records its reviewer and the skill version
steps.text:
*Independent.*

Intake adds the reviewer (git's `user.email` where the review is recorded, or the page's viewer) and
the reelplanning version that built the video to every review in `reviews/`. Old reviews are left as
they are. Without the version, a change to the skill can't be told apart from a change in the plans;
without the reviewer, one person's taste can't be told apart from what works.

steps.title: The repo's memory: `reel status` says what reviews show
steps.text:
*Needs step 1 (to tell reviewers apart; works without it for one reviewer).*

`reel status` ends with at most five lines, worked out each time from the ledger and `reviews/`:
how often a recommendation was taken; the questions answered in own words, and why; the steps
rewound, and those rewound again after a revision; the quick checks answered wrong; the misses (step
4). Each line has an id, and `reel memory <id>` prints its evidence: the reviews, the words, the
times. The skill says to read it before writing a plan and when tagging calls. Nothing is stored
that the reviews do not already hold.

steps.title: Your memory, across repos
steps.text:
*Needs step 1.*

When a review is recorded, a short summary of it (verdict, own-words answers and their reasons,
rewinds, wrong quick checks, the kinds of call flagged) is appended to a file of your own, outside
any repo (question 1). `reel memory --you` works out the same few lines across every repo you have
reviewed in: your taste, not this repo's facts. The skill reads both.

steps.title: Misses decide what stops
steps.text:
*Needs step 2.*

A miss is something a later plan, fix or system-video review changed that an earlier review let
through: a decision superseded, an accepted call later flagged or reversed, a part reworked soon
after. `reel memory` traces each to the question or call that passed it, and its kind (a call's
tags, a question's topic). A call of that kind stops the walkthrough again, whatever its streak of
accepts (D-084's rule gains this one exception), and the next plan that touches that part asks that
kind of question.

steps.title: A retro you start, checked against a fixed benchmark
steps.text:
*Needs steps 2–4.*

`reel status` suggests a retro when one is due (question 2). `reel retro` starts a plan: skill edits
the evidence supports, each citing it, adding no text the evidence does not need (not a quota to cut:
the owner's review, D-107's comment, asks only that nothing is added for its own sake). It is
reviewed like any plan. Before it is accepted, the benchmark (the Bob Dylan example, redone from the
same prompt, next to its text and HTML baselines) is run with the old and the new skill and
compared, so the retro is judged by something outside the loop's own numbers.

prerequisites.title: reelplanning: the whole system
prerequisites.gives: what the parts are and how a review goes

glossary.meaning: Turns plan.md into a video via HyperFrames
Voices the script, only the lines that changed since the last build; reelplanning build runs it, then finish-project and verify
The assembly tail: captions → index → plan-map → the terms index (which video explains each word) → plan-diff → the details check
Content-hash diff vs. the last committed build
<reelplanning-player>: where you watch, answer on the frame, mark, and press Finish
reelplanning review: serves the review page, takes the review when you press Send, keeps it in the inbox and hands it on once; sends the notifications
The agent's command from config.json, started by the review server when no session is waiting; auto mode, inside the sandbox, or without it (and the reviewer told) where this machine can't run it
scripts/reel.mjs; manages .reelplanning/; reel record logs a review's answers and files the review; reel status ends with memory
Acts on a plan review: approved, folds the comments into plan.md; changes requested, rewrites the steps a comment touched
Implements plan.md and logs each call the plan did not cover into walkthrough.md, with tags; its diff is then checked by a second, fresh agent (the code check)
Acts on a walkthrough review: changes the code for each flagged call; on changes requested, rebuilds only those beats
One video explaining the whole repo from spec.md; rebuilt where the spec changes
One pass by a reviewer, filed once as reviews/<kind>-<time>.json with a .md of what to act on; never overwritten. The player's download is annotations.json until it is filed

definedIn.title: Review loop, steps 3–4: record, then revise

glossary.meaning: The verdict at Finish. Approve (on a walkthrough, the build is accepted): the comments are acted on, no new video. Request changes: they are acted on, the touched beats rebuilt, and the video shown again

definedIn.title: Review loop, steps 1–2: finish, then send

glossary.meaning: .reelplanning/inbox/: reviews the review server has taken, each handed on once; not committed

The fence a headless run starts in: commands write only inside the repo, a hook keeps the file tools there too; checked before each run, and turned off, with the reviewer told, where it can't run (the hook stays)
A desktop notice from the review server: a video is ready, with what it will ask, or a headless run has ended

definedIn.title: Review loop, steps 5–6: rebuild, and you're told

glossary.meaning: A choice the agent made on its own while building, one the plan did not cover: one row in walkthrough.md. Labelled visible, hard-to-undo or close when you might want to overturn it

Which choices stop the walkthrough video: an off-plan change always, an unlabelled choice never, a labelled one until you have accepted that label ten times in a row, or again after a recent late fix with that label

definedIn.title: Build loop, step 3: the walkthrough video

glossary.meaning: What reviews show, worked out each time from the ledger and reviews/, never kept by hand: the lines reel status ends with, the evidence behind each in reel memory <id>; the reviewer's own, across repos, from ~/.reelplanning/you.jsonl (--you)
A late fix: something a review let through that a later plan, fix or review had to change. A recent one makes choices with its label stop the video again, however many were accepted in a row

A label the agent puts on a choice it made alone, saying why you might want to look at it. Four kinds: *visible* (you'll notice it when you use the thing), *hard-to-undo* (changing it later costs real work), *close* (a toss-up: the other way was nearly as good), *deviation* (an off-plan change). A labelled choice stops the walkthrough video; an unlabelled one does not

definedIn.title: Build loop, step 1: build, and log each call

glossary.meaning: How many times in a row you accepted choices with the same label. At ten accepted in a row, choices with that label no longer stop the video; one flag starts the count again from zero

definedIn.title: Build loop, step 3: the walkthrough video

glossary.meaning: An off-plan change: a choice where the agent did something other than what the plan said. It always stops the walkthrough video

definedIn.title: Build loop, step 1: build, and log each call

glossary.meaning: One scene of a video: a picture and a sentence or two of its voice. A video is a row of scenes; a question or a choice pauses at the end of its scene
A stretch of one video under one title; the player shows "Chapter 2 of 4" as it begins, and N / P jump between them. Not a plan's step, and not a part of the system
One part of the system, drawn as a box: the review player, the review server and the rest of this table's ids. system.json calls it a component; the system video says "part"
A plan of skill edits the memory's evidence supports, started by reel retro when reel status says one is due, and judged against a fixed benchmark
One scene per chapter for the choices that don't stop: each can be flagged, and Accept all takes the rest

definedIn.title: Build loop, step 3: the walkthrough video

glossary.meaning: One numbered part of a plan: one change, what it does and what it needs from another step (### Step N in plan.md); the video tells each in its own scenes. The system video tells its two loops in steps too
Where a review ends: you approve, or ask for changes, and send what you answered and marked

definedIn.title: Review loop, steps 1–2: finish, then send

glossary.meaning: decisions.md: every answer you gave and every choice you accepted, one entry each, numbered across the repo (D-056); an entry is never edited, only added to or marked superseded

definedIn.title: Review loop, steps 3–4: record, then revise

glossary.meaning: A question on what the plan or the code will do; "Expected something else?" sends your words to the agent as a comment

The answer bar. A question is answered on the frame's cards when it has them (own words, a note, Accept / Flag beside them); a frame with no cards gets the bar in the lowest eighth it leaves empty (data-band="bottom"), and only an older video without that gets it under the video; the video never changes size
Files a review of the system video and sorts each comment: fix the video, a small change, or a new plan

definedIn.title: Build loop, step 6: this video catches up

glossary.meaning: A page a beat opens beside the paused video, for what the video cannot hold; started from a template in templates/details/
